paper: Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers
key_finding: 6-month/6-month relative-strength strategy earns ~12.0%/yr compounded (~1%/month); 12m/3m best at 1.31%/month; cumulative gain peaks ~9.5% at month 12 and partly reverses (~4% by month 36).
decay_caveats: Persisted in the 1990s (JT 2001, JF 56(2)). Our data: UMD 9.9%/yr in JT's sample vs 4.7%/yr after publication (-53%). Crash-prone (see Daniel & Moskowitz).

paper: Value and Momentum Everywhere
key_finding: Value and momentum premia in every asset class; value-momentum correlation about -0.6 within stock markets; global 50/50 value+momentum combination Sharpe 1.45.
decay_caveats: Standalone Sharpe ratios slightly lower in 1992-2011 than 1972-1991; gross of costs; value then suffered its 2007-2020 drawdown.

paper: Momentum Crashes
sample: US 1927-2013 + international equities and other asset classes
key_finding: Crashes happen in 'panic' states (after market falls, high volatility) when markets rebound: Mar-May 2009 losers +163% vs winners +8%; Jul-Aug 1932 losers +232% vs winners +32%. Dynamic weighting roughly doubles alpha and Sharpe.
decay_caveats: Constant-volatility scaling is an alternative fix (Barroso & Santa-Clara 2015, JFE 116(1)). Our data: UMD -49% in Mar-May 2009; worst drawdown -78% (1932-39).

paper: The Cross-Section of Expected Stock Returns
key_finding: Beta has no reliable relation to average returns; B/M decile returns rise from 0.30% to 1.83%/month (spread 1.53%/month); size and B/M absorb E/P and leverage effects.
decay_caveats: Our data: HML 5.1%/yr in FF's sample vs 2.2%/yr after publication (-57%). Fama & French (2021, RAPS 11(1):105-121): value premium much lower in the second half of 1963-2019, but too volatile to reject equal expected premia.

paper: Common Risk Factors in the Returns on Stocks and Bonds
key_finding: Three-factor model; HML 0.40%/month (t 2.91), SMB 0.27%/month (t 1.73).
decay_caveats: Size premium weak since (our data: SMB +2.2%/yr, t 1.7, 1963-2026; -0.8%/yr since 2010).

paper: A Five-Factor Asset Pricing Model
key_finding: Adds profitability (RMW) and investment (CMA); explains 71-94% of the cross-section variance of expected returns for test portfolios; HML redundant in this sample; HML only 0.21%/month (t 1.69) among big stocks vs 0.53% among small.
decay_caveats: Our data after publication (2015-05 to 2026-07): RMW 2.7%/yr (t 1.1; -15% vs in-sample), CMA -0.3%/yr (-108%).

paper: The Other Side of Value: The Gross Profitability Premium
key_finding: Gross profits/assets predicts returns about as well as B/M: value-weighted quintile spread 0.31%/month (t 2.49), FF3 alpha 0.52%/month (t 4.49); correlation with value -0.57, so combining improves both.
decay_caveats: Large caps alone: 0.26%/month (t 1.88), but large-cap profitability+value earns 0.62%/month (Sharpe 0.74). French's RMW uses operating, not gross, profitability.

paper: Quality Minus Junk
key_finding: Quality (profitable, growing, safe, well-managed) earns significant risk-adjusted returns: US QMJ alphas 39-60 bp/month (t 5.4-10.0), global 51-61 bp; quality stocks trade at only moderately higher prices.
decay_caveats: Raw top-minus-bottom decile spread only 42-52 bp/month (t ~2.5); much of the alpha comes from QMJ's low/negative beta. Authors are AQR-affiliated.

paper: Asset Growth and the Cross-Section of Stock Returns
key_finding: Low-minus-high total asset growth decile: ~20%/yr equal-weighted raw (~26% vs 6%), ~13%/yr value-weighted raw, ~8.4%/yr value-weighted risk-adjusted; effect holds among large caps.
decay_caveats: Now embedded in CMA/q-factor investment. Our data: CMA 5.5%/yr in CGS's sample vs 0.6%/yr after 2008 (-90%); -0.7%/yr since 2015.
verification: PARTLY (numbers from SSRN WP/secondary; JF abstract verified)

paper: Share Issuance and Cross-sectional Returns
sample: US, post-1970 (with an earlier comparison period)
key_finding: Post-1970, net share issuance predicts returns (negatively) more significantly than size, B/M or momentum; no significant predictive power in the earlier period for most horizons. Chen & Zimmermann replication 0.58%/month (t 4.9).
decay_caveats: Holds internationally (McLean, Pontiff & Watanabe 2009, JFE 94(1)). Our data: big-cap net repurchasers +1.5%/yr active 1963-2026, only +0.1%/yr since 2010.

paper: Market Reactions to Tangible and Intangible Information
key_finding: B/M predicts returns because it proxies for the 'intangible' (non-fundamental) part of past returns; a composite equity-issuance measure independently forecasts returns negatively.
decay_caveats: Numeric results not checked by R3.

paper: Do Stock Prices Fully Reflect Information in Accruals and Cash Flows about Future Earnings?
key_finding: Accruals are less persistent than cash flows, but prices act as if investors fixate on earnings; a low-minus-high accrual hedge earns 10.4% size-adjusted in year 1 (t 4.7), positive in 28 of 30 years.
decay_caveats: Green, Hand & Soliman (2011, Mgmt Sci 57(5):797-816): the hedge return decayed until it was no longer reliably positive. Our data: big-cap low-accrual quintile +1.9%/yr active 1963-2026, +2.4%/yr since 2010 (t 1.6).

paper: Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift: Delayed Price Response or Risk Premium?
key_finding: Prices keep drifting in the direction of the earnings surprise for ~60 trading days: extreme SUE deciles about +/-2% each (~4% long-short per quarter, ~18% annualized).
decay_caveats: Chordia, Goyal, Sadka, Sadka & Shivakumar (2009, FAJ 65(4)): drift 0.04%/month in the most liquid stocks vs 2.43% in the least, and costs absorb 70-100% of paper profits.

paper: Rest in Peace Post-Earnings Announcement Drift
key_finding: Earnings surprises are now fully priced on the announcement day: the drift has been insignificant for large stocks since ~2006 and more recently for microcaps too.
decay_caveats: Text-based surprises still show drift (Meursault, Liang, Routledge & Scanlon 2023, JFQA 58(6):2299-2326: 1-yr drift 8.0% text-based vs 4.6% classic SUE in 2010-2019, working-paper figures).

paper: Betting Against Beta
sample: US 1926-2012 + 19 international markets, Treasuries, credit, futures
key_finding: Long leveraged low-beta / short high-beta (BAB) has US Sharpe 0.78 and FF3 alpha 0.73%/month (t 7.4); the security market line is flatter than CAPM predicts in 18 of 19 markets.
decay_caveats: Novy-Marx & Velikov (2022, JFE 143(1):80-106): BAB's construction effectively equal-weights and loads on tiny stocks; its return is explained by profitability/investment tilts. Our data: big-cap low-beta quintile -0.6%/yr raw active (beta 0.70), CAPM alpha +1.4%/yr (t 1.7), 1963-2026.

paper: The Cross-Section of Volatility and Expected Returns
key_finding: Stocks with high idiosyncratic volatility (relative to FF3) earn very low returns: top-minus-bottom quintile -1.06%/month (value-weighted).
decay_caveats: Bali & Cakici (2008, JFQA 43(1):29-58): not robust to weighting, breakpoints, data frequency and size/price/liquidity screens. Our data: big-cap low-variance quintile -1.0%/yr raw active (beta 0.66), CAPM alpha +1.3%/yr (t 1.4), 1963-2026.

paper: Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability?
key_finding: Predictor portfolio returns are 26% lower out-of-sample (upper bound on data mining) and 58% lower after publication; 32% is attributed to publication-informed trading; bigger declines for predictors with higher in-sample returns.
decay_caveats: Implies keeping ~40% of in-sample premia for published signals. Our French check: -53% (momentum), -57% (value).

paper: ...and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns
key_finding: Once you account for how many factors have been tried, a newly proposed factor needs t > 3.0; most claimed research findings in financial economics are likely false.
decay_caveats: Companion Harvey & Liu (2015, JPM 42(1):13-28): the Sharpe-ratio haircut is nonlinear; the 50% rule of thumb is too lenient below Sharpe 0.4 and too harsh above 1.0.

paper: Replicating Anomalies
key_finding: With microcaps mitigated (NYSE breakpoints, value-weighted returns), 65% fail |t| >= 1.96 (including 96% of the trading-frictions category) and 82% fail t >= 2.78; replicated anomalies are much smaller than originally reported.
decay_caveats: Supports a large-cap, value-weighted implementation of only the robust families, with shrunken premia.

paper: Is There a Replication Crisis in Finance?
key_finding: With a Bayesian framework, most factors replicate (82.4% in the US), cluster into 13 themes, work out-of-sample internationally, and their evidence is strengthened (not weakened) by the large number of factors.
decay_caveats: Average alpha 0.49%/month in-sample vs 0.26% after the original samples (-47%): decay, not disappearance.

paper: Open Source Cross-Sectional Asset Pricing
key_finding: 98% of the 161 clearly significant predictors reproduce with t > 1.96; reproduced vs original t-stats slope 0.88.
decay_caveats: Reproduction is in-sample; it says nothing about post-publication returns.

paper: How Do Factor Premia Vary Over Time? A Century of Evidence
sample: Value, momentum, carry, defensive across 6 asset classes, ~1926-2020
key_finding: Pooled t-stats 5.1 (value) to >6.6 (defensive); multifactor Sharpe 1.46; out-of-sample Sharpe 49% below original-sample for value but only 18% lower for the multifactor combination; little evidence of arbitrage-driven decay.
decay_caveats: AQR authors; the long-short, multi-asset setting differs from large-cap long-only equities.

paper: Is (Systematic) Value Investing Dead?
sample: US equities, focus on the 2018-2020 value drawdown
key_finding: Value's recent underperformance came mainly from a widening gap between prices and fundamentals (valuation spreads), not from value's fundamentals failing.
decay_caveats: Decomposition numbers not checked.

paper: Reports of Value's Death May Be Greatly Exaggerated
key_finding: HML fell ~55% from 2007 to mid-2020; the change in relative valuations explains the entire drawdown; capitalising intangibles improves value.
decay_caveats: Our data: HML -57.8% peak-to-trough (2006-12 to 2020-09), then +68.5% from 2020-10 to 2022-12.

paper: The Role of Shorting, Firm Size, and Time on Market Anomalies
sample: 86 years US + ~40 years international equities and asset classes
key_finding: The long side supplies ~60% of value and ~half of momentum profits (almost all of size); the value premium falls with firm size and is weak among the largest stocks; momentum has no reliable size relation; variation over time looks like chance.
decay_caveats: Consistent with our large-cap long-only capture of ~45-54% of the all-cap combo premium.

paper: When Equity Factors Drop Their Shorts
key_finding: Both legs carry premia, but most added value comes from the long legs, and the shorts are largely subsumed by the longs, in large and small caps alike.
decay_caveats: Magnitudes not checked.

paper: A Taxonomy of Anomalies and Their Trading Costs
key_finding: Most anomalies with <50% monthly turnover keep significant net spreads with cost mitigation (buy/hold spreads); few high-turnover ones do; size, value and profitability have the largest capacity.
decay_caveats: Institutional live-trade costs are much lower (Frazzini, Israel & Moskowitz 2018 WP 'Trading Costs', SSRN 3229719); a small investor's costs sit between the two.

paper: Long-Only Style Investing: Don't Just Mix, Integrate
key_finding: Integrating styles in a single portfolio beats a mix of stand-alone style sleeves (higher return and IR) by avoiding stocks with offsetting exposures.
decay_caveats: AQR authors.

paper: Stocks for the Long Run? Evidence from a Broad Sample of Developed Markets
key_finding: A diversified investor with a 30-year horizon has a 12% chance of losing to inflation.
decay_caveats: Counterweight to US-only 'stocks always win over 20 years' evidence.
